A.explanation: Kinetic energy is $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$, not $\Delta p / \Delta t$. The value of momentum is not the same as its gradient.

B.explanation: Rate of change of kinetic energy is power, with unit $\text{W}$, while the gradient here has unit $\text{N}$.

C.explanation: Gradient is rate of change of momentum $dp/dt$, which by Newton's second law equals the resultant force.

D.explanation: For constant mass, $p = mv$ so velocity is proportional to the momentum value, not to the gradient of the momentum-time graph.

hints: Look at the axes of the curved graph: vertical is momentum $p$ and horizontal is time $t$, so the gradient at a time means $\Delta p / \Delta t$.
Recall the form of Newton's second law that links force to momentum: $F = dp/dt$ for the resultant force.
Check the unit of the gradient, $\text{kg m s}^{-1} / \text{s} = \text{N}$, and ask which of the four named quantities has unit of force.
walkthrough: Identify what gradient means on this graph: gradient = change in y divided by change in x = change in momentum divided by change in time, $\text{gradient} = \Delta p / \Delta t$.
State the governing law: Newton's second law can be written as resultant force equals rate of change of momentum, $F = dp/dt$.
Apply it to the graph: the tangent gradient at any particular time is therefore the instantaneous rate of change of momentum and equals the instantaneous resultant force.
Note the curve flattens, so the gradient and hence the resultant force decreases as the car speeds up, which is consistent with increasing resistive forces.
This matches the description resultant force on the car. This is option C.
